title: Agent Integration Trigger Response
description: The response a trigger returns, per Agent Integration Contract 3.3. This is the Discovery Contract 4 envelope with one payload key, `findings` - it is NOT a new response format, and every rule the envelope states applies here unchanged. The root is deliberately OPEN, matching discovery-envelope-v1: the envelope permits a new channel to add a payload key without a schema change forbidding it, and closing it here would contradict the document that admits `findings` in the first place. What this schema adds over the envelope is the closed vocabulary of a finding and the payload/absence coupling of 3.3.

schema_version.description: Surface-owned, per Discovery Contract 4. Independent of any package version and of the host protocol date.

ok.description: Surface-owned. A publisher cannot forge it: publisher bytes nest under a payload key and never reach this level.

present.description: true when the trigger has findings to report; false when it found nothing (4.1). NOTE the narrowed meaning: in the Discovery Contract `present: false` means the document does not exist, here it means THIS TRIGGER FOUND NOTHING. A consumer must not read it as evidence about what the package ships - that question is `list`'s to answer.

reason.description: Free text for humans, never a machine field (Discovery Contract 4.2). Required with `present: false` so a silent trigger still says why it was silent. Deliberately NOT a closed set: adding a machine-readable cause here would contradict the envelope rule for the convenience of a caller that should be asking `list` instead.

findings.description: Present only alongside `present: true`. An empty array is non-conforming - silence is the absent shape, not an empty payload (4.1).

task.description: The Consumption Map section that produced the finding, as the bare section number. Closed set: a caller routing on it needs one, and a task number is the only identifier the map guarantees is stable. Not free text.

level.description: The conformance vocabulary, NOT the check-severity vocabulary (LOW/MINOR/MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL), because the question a caller asks here is `may I proceed`, not `how bad is this`. ASSIGNED BY THE CONSUMER from the Consumer Conformance profile and NEVER read from shipped metadata (4.3) - a package that could set its own finding's level would be grading its own exam, and one that could raise an unrelated finding to `must` would be blocking a competitor. That constraint is behavioral and cannot be expressed in JSON Schema; it is enforced by MIRI-CONSUMER-051 and the E3 golden, not here.

summary.description: What was found, in the consumer's own words. May be derived from publisher content - content influence is permitted, control influence is not (4.3).

source.description: The served document the finding was drawn from, so a caller can attribute the claim rather than adopt it.

purl.description: The package the finding concerns. Optional because a finding may concern a step rather than a package.

quote.description: Publisher bytes, ATTRIBUTED RATHER THAN ADOPTED (MIRI-CONSUMER-020, MIRI-CONSUMER-022). A consumer rendering this must not present it as its own assertion. It is the one field in a finding whose contents a hostile publisher controls outright.

allOf.description: 3.3: a response MUST NOT carry `present: true` with no `findings` key.
3.3: a response MUST NOT carry `findings` alongside `present: false`. 4.1: silence carries a reason.
